Bengaluru: Precision oncology firm, 4baseCare has collaborated with Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) to expand its clinical database to over 80,000 records.As part of the collaboration, the firm will integrate clinical data from a select cohort of cancer patients into its AI-powered oncology platform, OncoTwin, allowing oncologists to examine treatments and outcomes among clinically comparable cancer patients.

According to 4baseCare, OncoTwin is designed to create a digital twin of a cancer patient using their genomic and clinical information. “The platform identifies patients with comparable disease characteristics in its reference datasets, including the MSK records, and examines the treatments, drug combinations and observed outcomes associated with those cases allowing oncologists to consider how similar patients have been treated in clinical practice, alongside established treatment guidelines and their own clinical judgement,” it explained.

Advt

The integration will give OncoTwin access to a combined evidence base of approximately more than 80,000 patient records. These clinical records will support data-driven cancer treatment decisions across 4baseCare’s network of hospitals and oncologists, the firm said.4baseCare expects to launch the expanded OncoTwin Platform in its existing markets in India, Latin America and Southeast Asia from January next year.

It currently works with over 1000 hospitals and 2500 oncologists across its network. Hitesh Goswami, Co-founder & CEO, 4baseCare, said, “This collaboration seeks to address a major challenge in cancer care. While advances in medical science have made cancer treatment more precise, oncologists still face difficulties in using the vast amount of information available from other cancer patients to determine the most suitable treatment for an individual. With OncoTwin, we want to make that pool of information useful to oncologists across the world. The integration of MSK’s deidentified patient data, alongside our growing Indian dataset, is a significant step towards that goal.”

Rick Peng, Lead, Digital Ventures, MSK’s Office of Entrepreneurship and Commercialization, said, “Building on our work with 4baseCare as a participant in our iHub Challenge accelerator cohort in 2025, we're excited for this expansion of our contributions towards 4baseCare's efforts for a common mission of ending cancer worldwide.”
